claim: Cross-border real-time payments (SPEI, FPS, UPI corridors) presented as a live CashPro sub-product
finding: BofA announced the service on Jun 4 2026 as 'expected to launch next quarter'. On Sep 29 2026 PYMNTS reported only a completed pilot (Bradesco, Brazil to Hong Kong FPS, over Swift) and said the solution 'will later be made available through CashPro'. No public source shows general availability in CashPro as of Nov 6 2026.
resolution: Sub-product retained but labelled announced/pilot; GA not confirmed as of 2026-11-06.

claim: Initiate wire (SWIFT) or real-time (SPEI/FPS/UPI) via CashPro or Swift messaging
finding: The real-time corridors are a pilot / pre-launch capability (see BAC-C001); the step reads as a live option.
resolution: System_behavior notes pilot status; SWIFT wire is the live path.

claim: 2025–26: cross-border real-time payments to Mexico (SPEI), UK (FPS), India (UPI) via CashPro/Swift announced [S027]
finding: Announcement is dated Jun 4 2026 (not 2025) and a Sep 29 2026 pilot with Bradesco (Brazil→Hong Kong FPS) followed; Hong Kong FPS corridor missing.
resolution: Replaced with dated Jun 4 2026 announcement + Sep 29 2026 Bradesco pilot entry.

claim: Commercial leadership: TCH co-owner, first to enable $10M RTP, Recipient Select/Global Digital Disbursements with Zelle/Venmo/PayPal/Interac/Pay to Card, 100+ CashPro APIs, Coalition Greenwich No. 1 digital channels four years running [S025,S052,S053,S071,S049]
finding: The Jun 10 2025 release says BofA is 'one of the first financial institutions' to enable the $10M limit, not the first. TCH co-ownership and the 32% week-1-to-week-6 growth (chart description) are confirmed.
resolution: 'one of the first to enable $10M RTP'.

claim: Zelle scam intake is phone/Security-Center only – the FAQ offers no in-app scam-report path and reimbursement criteria remain 'qualifying imposter scams' [S901,S915]
finding: The Security Center's Report Suspicious Activity page lists 'Log into Online Banking or call' for ATM, debit, check & Zelle. So intake is not phone-only. No mobile-app or in-app claim submission is described for Zelle, and the FAQ still only links out.
resolution: Intake via Online Banking or phone; no mobile in-app scam-report path documented.

claim: Mobile deposit exceptions communicated by postal letter; deposit-holds FAQ page not loadable [S006,S038]
finding: The gap-fill pass rendered the Deposit Holds FAQ (S903). The chapter itself now cites it for in-flow hold disclosure (confirmation screen, email alert). The postal-letter path is still confirmed on the Mobile Check Deposit page.
resolution: Weakness rewritten without the 'not loadable' clause.

claim: Recipient notified; unenrolled Zelle recipients get enrollment prompt (up to 3 business days)
finding: Digital Disbursements page: unenrolled recipients enroll 'in a few easy steps'. The 'minutes or up to three business days' footnote applies to Zelle payment delivery in general, not to the enrollment window.

claim: Tag must be tied to a U.S. mobile number (sources S020, S013); tag created via mobile Request flow
finding: The claim is true but is not in S020 or S013. The Zelle FAQ (S901) states it. S901 also says tags can be created in mobile OR online banking, at first enrollment or later from Zelle settings, which the journey omits.
resolution: Claim kept; sources S020,S901; web creation path appended.

claim: Mar 31 2025: Zelle standalone app retired – BofA page directs users to enroll through participating banks (2,300+/2,400+) [S002,S057]
finding: The retirement itself is well reported by third parties. The BofA Zelle page (S002) does not mention the retirement, though. It only says 'No need to download another app'.
resolution: Reworded to network-wide retirement; attribution corrected.

claim: Zelle Forward pilot (Mar 2026): donor-advised-fund grants disbursed to nonprofits over Zelle via BofA Charitable Gift Fund – first such Zelle use case [S922]
finding: 'Zelle® Forward' is the Zelle network's innovation agenda, not the pilot's name. The pilot is a limited Donor-Advised-Fund proof of concept through BofA Charitable Gift Fund that is 'not currently available across the Zelle Network'. 'First-of-its-kind' is the release's own wording.

claim: Chapter lists no automatic round-up savings transfer product
finding: Keep the Change is live. It rounds debit-card purchases up to the next dollar and moves the change daily from checking to the enrolled savings account. Enrollment is through Online Banking.
resolution: New sub-product BAC-P02-S03 Keep the Change®.

claim: Chapter lists no overdraft-protection sweep transfer product
finding: Balance Connect® for overdraft protection automatically transfers available funds from up to five linked backup accounts. There is no transfer fee, and customers enroll in the Mobile Banking app or Online Banking. The small-business FAQ describes it for business accounts too.

claim: Business Advantage 360 has no dual approval or per-user limits: the sub-user demo exposes only view/transact toggles per account and Full/Limited Bill Pay access [S906]
finding: This rests on absence of evidence (a sub-user demo and the features page), yet it is stated as fact. The Business Services Addendum shows an approval role did exist: the P and I Administrator could 'approve bills, authorize and schedule payments'. That Payments and Invoicing service is 'not open for new enrollment'. No public page settles whether BA360 core payments (Wire/ACH, Bill Pay) support dual approval.
resolution: Reworded as 'no public documentation' (INFERRED) with legacy P&I note.

finding: The bank's own Zelle page and FAQ confirm participation, and BofA is an EWS owner bank.

claim: value: 'commercial only (Recipient Select Pay to Card); no consumer debit-card instant transfer found'
finding: The value is free text, not a boolean or 'unknown', and it conflicts with the participation baseline participation (push_to_card 'unknown'). Recipient Select does list 'Pay to Card' (bank page).

claim: Consumer RTP RFP UI location 'not documented'
finding: The Service Agreement §5.E documents where to cancel: 'going to the Transfers section of the Bank of America website or mobile app and tapping on Activity'. It also states consumer RTP limits ($3,500 / 10 per 24h; $10,000 / 30 per 7 days; $20,000 / 60 per month), that there is no fee, and 'We do not offer a protection program for authorized payments made through RTP.'
resolution: Touchpoint/limits/no-protection added; inbox location remains open.

claim: Still not a FedNow participant as of the 11/02/26 Federal Reserve list, while JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citi, Capital One and PNC are listed [S917]
finding: Re-parsed the Fed XLSX (updated 11/02/26, file modified 2026-11-03). Bank of America is absent, which confirms the claim. U.S. Bank ('US BANK, NA') is also listed alongside JPM, WF, Citi, Capital One and PNC; Truist is absent.

claim: no Same Day ACH option (consumer external transfers) [S013,S016]
finding: Challenge: the participation baseline marks same_day_ach_origination=true for BofA, which suggests the 'no Same Day ACH' weakness is wrong.
resolution: Original weakness stands: the the participation baseline flag refers to commercial (CashPro) Same Day ACH origination, which the chapter records under BAC-P13-S01; consumer external transfers have no Same Day ACH option.
